title: Cambricon-LLM: A Chiplet-Based Hybrid Architecture for On-Device Inference of 70B LLM
problem: Deploying 70B LLMs on edge devices requires handling single-batch inference with extremely low arithmetic intensity, creating severe memory footprint and bandwidth demands that exceed limited edge device resources. The fundamental challenge is managing the vast parameter-to-bandwidth gap on memory-constrained devices.
motivation: On-device LLM inference preserves user privacy, improves network resilience, and enables intelligent edge capabilities on devices like smartphones and robotics without cloud dependency.
method: Cambricon-LLM uses a chiplet-based architecture (multiple specialized chips working together) that combines an NPU (a processor designed for AI) with a dedicated NAND flash storage chip. They use a hardware-tiling strategy—a way of arranging data into blocks that minimize how much data has to move between the NPU and flash, saving time and power. The NAND flash has two advanced features: in-flash computing (it can do simple calculations right where the data is stored) and on-die ECC (error-checking built directly into the storage chips). The NPU handles the big matrix multiplications and special computations, while the flash handles lighter processing tasks directly on itself.
key_novelty: The single core idea is putting computing capability directly inside NAND flash storage—not just in the separate NPU—so the flash and NPU can work together without having to constantly move data between them.
contributions: Chiplet-based hybrid architecture combining NPU and NAND flash for on-device 70B LLM inference
Hardware-tiling strategy to minimize data movement overhead between NPU and NAND flash
In-flash computing and on-die ECC techniques for efficient lightweight processing within flash storage
Demonstrates 22-45× speedup over existing flash-offloading technologies

metrics.speedup: 22-45× faster than flash-offloading; 3.44 token/s for 70B LLM, 36.34 token/s for 7B LLM

limitations: Limitations not discussed in the abstract.
primary_theme: Edge LLM inference via flash-augmented NPU chiplet
